source_user: Choose between tensor and pipeline parallelism for a latency-sensitive multi-GPU service. State the assumptions needed. Scenario variant 234: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: compare per-GPU memory, communication topology, layer partitioning, batch and microbatch behavior, synchronization, latency target, and failure/reconfiguration costs.
corrected_answer: Scenario variant 234: do not choose tensor parallelism (TP) or pipeline parallelism (PP) from the prompt alone. Assume the model graph, layer shapes, precision, parameter and activation memory, GPU count/type and usable HBM (GiB), topology/link bandwidth, software versions, clocks, request lengths, arrival rate, concurrency, batching policy, and latency/throughput/error/quality/availability SLO thresholds are specified; label estimates and measured facts. Enumerate topology-aware TP degrees and balanced PP stage partitions, rejecting configurations without positive memory headroom or a feasible failure/recovery plan. Hypothesis: on identical hardware and a representative fixed workload, the feasible configuration with lower held-out p99 end-to-end latency while meeting every SLO gate is superior; falsify this if p99 is not lower or any gate fails. Warm up, randomize paired trials, tune only on disjoint data, then evaluate held-out requests while holding workload mix, arrival rate, precision, clocks, concurrency, and batch policy constant. Measure compute, TP collectives or PP activation transfers, synchronization wait, stage imbalance, pipeline bubbles, queueing, throughput, TTFT, TPOT, p50/p95/p99 latency, errors, quality, availability, memory headroom, and recovery time in stated units with confidence intervals. Control for cache state, thermals, background load, sequence-length mix, warmup, retries, stragglers, and request scheduler; report microbatch count and batch-size effects rather than assuming larger batches help. Canary the selected design only with authorization and isolation, preserve the known-good deployment, and roll back on any SLO breach, error/quality regression, memory pressure, or recovery failure. Without measurements, the conclusion is provisional and no universal TP/PP winner is justified.
risks: Missing platform facts and SLO thresholds prevent a universal winner.
Tail latency is sensitive to batching, queueing, stage imbalance, collectives, stragglers, retries, and workload drift.

Repeated randomized paired trials with disjoint tuning and held-out p50/p95/p99, TTFT, TPOT, throughput, error, quality, and availability results.
